legalFramework.description: Common commercial policy is an EU exclusive competence under TFEU Article 3(1)(e), subject to treaty-specific limits and mixed-agreement distinctions.
Shared competence includes areas enumerated in TFEU Article 4; classify each instrument by legal basis rather than broad policy labels.
TFEU Article 216 provides the basis for EU international agreements in specified circumstances; existence of authority does not mean every bilateral member-state action is an EU action.
EU–Japan Strategic Partnership Agreement is a mixed agreement involving the EU and its member states; full entry into force January 2025.

attributionRules.test: EU institution acted within its competence and the instrument is attributable to the Union; report Union-level action only.
National government bilateral instrument without EU co-signature or delegated EU competence; attribute to named country, not automatically to EU.
EU and member states are parties; retain mixed scope, avoid duplicating the event as multiple independent geopolitical outcomes.
Separate legal entry into force, financial disbursement, national implementation, and independent partner outcome.
Do not add EU institution totals to member-state totals without eliminating overlap and harmonizing units.

openGaps: Identify treaty-specific EU and national competences in implementation instruments
Gather EU and national expenditure on matching time and cost definitions
Find independently measured partner policy outcomes and counterfactual
Separate formal EU external policy from national bilateral diplomacy
limitations: Legal competence classification does not establish political leverage or influence.
EU-wide and member-state-only agreements are not interchangeable samples.
No diplomatic influence scores or audit gate promotion.
